name: sw_get
description: Reads the whole document. format: "latex" (default), "markdown", "json" (the editor's own format).

name: sw_outline
description: The document's blocks: for each, its number (index), kind, first words and formulas (a displayed formula's \label as label). Use it to find a block's number before changing that block.

name: sw_set
description: Replaces the whole document with LaTeX (a full document or just the body).

name: sw_insert
description: Inserts LaTeX (paragraphs, formulas, lists, theorems...) after block index; without index it goes at the end; index = -1 puts it at the start.

name: sw_replaceBlock
description: Replaces block index with LaTeX.

name: sw_deleteBlock
description: Deletes block index.

name: sw_find
description: Finds text (not inside formulas); returns the block number of each place.

name: sw_replace
description: Replaces the text find with with (not inside formulas); all = false replaces only the first.

name: sw_formulas
description: Lists all formulas (inline and displayed) with their block numbers, and the \label of a displayed formula that has one.

name: sw_setFormula
description: Changes formula n (in the order formulas gives) to new LaTeX.

name: sw_undo
description: Undoes the last step.

name: sw_redo
description: Redoes.

name: sw_open
description: Opens a file: in the desktop app give path (.sci or a 5.x .tex). The file is not opened where it is: it is imported, that is copied with the files it uses (pictures, sub-documents, .bib) into a project folder of its own in the projects folder (aiFolder in info), and the copy is the open document; the file you named is never written. The answer is as info gives it (path is the copy), with imported: { from, folder, copied, notFound, notCopied }. A file imported before: its existing copy is opened instead, and the note says so and whether the original has changed since; fresh = true imports it again as a new copy. If no earlier import has this path but one has the same file name and the same contents, the file is imported all the same, and alike: { importedFrom, on, copy } with the note tell you of that copy (it may be this file under another path, such as a network drive; then go on in that copy). A file of a project (a folder of the projects folder that has opensw's records) is opened as it is; any other file is imported, also one in another folder of the projects folder or in a project's records. When it is open in the editor already it is not read again but brought to the screen as it is there, unsaved changes and all (alreadyOpen: true, and the note says so). Without asking only files in the projects folder, the open document's folder and the folders the user allowed; anywhere else the user is asked first. It takes the place of the document on screen, unless that one has unsaved changes: then it stays open too (see documents).

name: sw_documents
description: The documents open in the editor (its Window menu). For each: doc (its number; 0 is the one on screen, which all the other commands work on), name, path, and changed (true: it has changes that are not saved).

name: sw_switchTo
description: Brings open document doc (its number in documents) to the screen, so that the other commands work on it. The numbers change with it: the answer is the new list, as documents gives it.

name: sw_close
description: Closes open document doc (its number in documents); without doc, the one on screen. A document with unsaved changes is not closed: save it first, or give discard = true and the user is asked whether its changes may be lost. The answer is the list of the documents still open (when the last one is closed, a new empty one).

name: sw_save
description: Saves (desktop app): the main format is 5.x .tex (5.5 opens it); a path ending in .sci saves as .sci. Without path it saves back to the same file in its project folder (keeping a .bak; an unchanged 5.x file is not rewritten; in an edited one only the edited parts are written again, the rest stays as it was in the file). A LaTeX file 5.x did not write (info: from55 false) is written as a 5.x file over the copy in the project folder; the LaTeX as it was imported stays in the project's records. What is edited is always in the projects folder (aiFolder in info), and this command saves there and nowhere else: a path in the document's own project folder makes that file the open document; a path anywhere else in the projects folder gives the document a new project folder of its own (the first save of a new document needs such a path). A path outside the projects folder is refused, and so is saving a document that was opened in place outside it: this command writes nothing out there, so the original a document was imported from can never be written by it, under whatever name. A copy outside the projects folder is for the user to make (File > Save As). A project's records are never saved to. The answer's path is the open document; note says when that is not the file you named. Only .tex and .sci.

name: sw_records
description: The records of the open document's project folder (desktop app); read them before your first edit. Returns folder, files (the paths of the three records), changeLog (the last entries of Change log.txt, about 60 lines: the import, every AI change with the blocks before and after, every save; opensw writes it, and counts blocks from 1 where the commands count from 0), fileMap (File map.txt: what is in the folder, where the document was imported from, what it uses) and handoff (the last three notes of Handoff notes.txt, left by the AI that worked on the document before).

name: sw_handoff
description: Adds a note to Handoff notes.txt in the open document's project folder, for whoever goes on with the work (a person or another AI): what you set out to do, what is done, what is left. Plain English, a few lines. Write one before you finish; opensw puts the date and time above it.

name: sw_typeset
description: Typesets to PDF and opens it (desktop app). Returns pdf (its path) and errors (what TeX reported). With errors the PDF still comes out but those parts may be wrong, so fix them (the message gives the line of the TeX).

name: sw_info
description: The document's name, path, number of blocks and formulas, from55 (it is a Scientific Word 5.x file; false for other LaTeX, a .sci or a new document), and aiFolder: the projects folder, where the documents are kept (each in a folder of its own) and AI may always open and save without asking. For a document in a project folder also project: { folder, importedFrom (the file it was copied from; never written), records (the folder of its records, see records) } and handoff: the latest handoff note.

name: sw_compute
description: Computes one formula with the computation engine (SymPy with Giac and FriCAS; Mathematica first when it is chosen in Tools > Engine Setup), without changing the document. op: evaluate (default), numeric, simplify, expand, factor, combine, rewrite_exp, rewrite_sincos, solve, numericsolve, ode, odenumeric (Solve ODE > Numeric: a one-column matrix of equations (any order) and initial values y(0) = 1, y'(0) = 0; defines the solutions as functions, so y(1) can then be evaluated), check, partialfractions (params: [variable], when there are several), collect, differentiate (params: [variable, times]), integrate, series (params: [variable, number of terms, point], in this order; as in 5.5 the terms are counted from the lowest power, default 5: 1/(1-x) ends in O(x^5); point default 0), extrema, laplace, inverselaplace, fourier, determinant, inverse, transpose, eigenvalues, rank, rref, nullspace, trace, charpoly, adjugate, mean, median, variance, stddev, implicitdiff, integersolve, recursion (a one-column matrix: the recurrence and starting values), maximize, minimize, feasible, standardize, dual (simplex method: a one-column matrix, first row the objective, the other rows the constraints, all variables >= 0), gradient, divergence, curl, laplacian, hessian, jacobian, wronskian, potential, vectorpotential (params are the basis variables, default x, y, z), byparts (params: [u]), changevar (params: ["u=g(x)"]), approxint (params: [method, number of subintervals]; method is left, midpoint, right, trapezoid or simpson, in single quotes), iterate (params: [starting value, count]); and the rest of the Compute menu of 5.5, each as ENGINE.md describes its params: cholesky, plu, qr, svd, singularvalues, jordan, hermite, smith, rationalcanonical, ffgauss, gauss, minpoly, eigenvectors, colbasis, rowbasis, concat, stack, reshape, fillmatrix, randommatrix, condition, definiteness, norm, orthogonal, permanent, spectralradius, htranspose, rewrite_rational, rewrite_float, rewrite_factorial, rewrite_gamma, rewrite_log, rewrite_sinhcosh, rewrite_sin, rewrite_cos, rewrite_tan, rewrite_arcsin, rewrite_arccos, rewrite_arctan, rewrite_arccot, rewrite_polar, rewrite_rectangular, rewrite_normal, combine_exp, combine_log, combine_powers, combine_trig, combine_arctan, combine_hyp, eqs_to_matrix, matrix_to_eqs, mode, geomean, harmonicmean, meandev, moment, quantile, correlation, covariance, fitcurve, randomnumbers, divide, roots, sort, companion, interpret, inversefourier, odelaplace, odeseries. Returns the result as LaTeX; solve, numericsolve, integersolve, ode, extrema, maximize, minimize return a list of solutions.

name: sw_engine
description: The computation engine of the Compute menu (Tools > Engine Setup). Without engine: which one is chosen, the ones that can be chosen (available: id and name; sympy is SymPy with Giac and FriCAS, which comes with opensw; others, such as mathematica, are programs on this computer, desktop app only) and versions (what the chosen engine reports, loading it first). With engine (an id from available): chooses it for every document, as the dialog does, and answers the same. error: the chosen engine could not be started; notice: the Python that comes with opensw did not start, so SymPy runs in the slower Pyodide.

name: sw_steps
description: The derivation steps. Every displayed formula can be a step with a fixed name (of several rows, as in align or eqnarray, a row that starts with = goes on from the row before); the names, what each step uses and its last check are kept in a file beside the document (<document>.steps.json), so the document is not changed (a formula with a \label is named by the label). Returns for each step: name, block, status (pass, fail, unknown, unchecked: never checked or changed since the check, trusted), why, uses, waitsFor; ready: the open steps that can be worked on now; problems. With name: that one step in full (formula, extra checks, what the engine was asked and what it answered).

name: sw_nameSteps
description: Gives every displayed formula without a name the next free one (s1, s2 ...), kept in the steps file. inDocument = true also writes each step's name into the document as the formula's \label (5.5 shows a label as a marker).

name: sw_setStep
description: Sets what a step is checked with; only the arguments given change. uses: the names of the steps and given groups whose definitions it needs (a step defines the names its formula starts with, as w_0 = ...; only the ones listed are in force, not theirs in turn). note: a few words on what the step says. trust: why it is taken as true without a check ("" removes it). extra: checks for what the formula does not spell out, each { latex, equals, why, op?, params? }: latex (or what the compute operation op makes of it) must equal equals; @1, @2 stand for the last side of the formula's 1st, 2nd statement. block: gives this name to the displayed formula in that block (for a name whose formula was rewritten; a name the formula had before goes).

name: sw_setGiven
description: A group of definitions the problem gives, for steps to use by its name: defs such as "a=2", "f(x)=x^2". An empty list removes the group.

name: sw_checkSteps
description: Checks the steps (all, or only names) with the computation engine and keeps the results in the steps file. Each equality a = b of the formula and each extra check is asked as "a - b simplifies to 0" with only the definitions of what the step uses in force (the user's own definitions are set aside and put back); a = b + O(x^n) is asked as: a - b and its first n - 1 derivatives are 0 at x = 0. A name the document defines but the step does not use gives unknown, with the name. Answers as steps does.

name: sw_select
description: Puts the cursor in block block.

name: sw_focusEnd
description: Puts the cursor at the end of the document.
